doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Lionel Hampton audition on the job
summary: Probably recommended by Curley Hamner, Hampton auditioned by playing a concert without rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Were you recruited by Lionel? How did that happen? How’d you get there?

Let’s see. I’m trying to think of who got me that job in the band, because there were a lot of musicians in the band at that time that were jazz players. It could have been Curley Hamner. That was the other guy that was the drummer in the band, and danced. He was a tap dancer. He and I were very close. He could have been the one that recommended me for the band. I took the audition.
Auditions at that time were: you would go on a concert stage and play the music without a rehearsal. That was the audition.
So there was a gig, and you played the gig.

You had to play a gig. That was the audition. So you had to be able to read. You had to be able to not play when you shouldn’t be playing. All that was part of what made them decide that they wanted to have you there.
